In the short amount of time since i have gotten this game, it has quickly become one of my favorite games. Even in early access, there is plenty of content to keep me occupied for 100 hour and I'm not half way done with the content this game has for me. I would recommend checking this game out if you enjoy rogue lite style games or even if you want to just try the genre.
Incredibly underrated! One of my top games to play and my time is low cause I mostly play on the steam deck. Honestly amazing just buy it
good amount of content, and smooth movement, looks promising in alpha, looking forward for whats to come.
I still liked Rogue Legacy 1 better. While I think this one has more mechanics. Both great games btw.

Fantastic sequel to the best action roguelite of its era. The new systems are great, the difficulty is pretty smooth (easier dungeons and far more challenging bosses than before), you need to go deep into the NG+7 to see all the bosses which takes a while, but it's been a blast.

The first Rogue Legacy was awesome, and thus one is nothing short of amazing.
Controls are tight, the game's mood is great, the lore is inviting, the mechanics are well made, there are plenty of secrets to find, what's not to love about that ?

First of all i love this kind of games... if you don't like 2D games you are wasting your time
but other than that this game is so fun for grinders and 2D lovers
Game play : 8/10
Music: 5/10 (repetitive)
Story: 6/10(narrating it would be awesome reading long passage is not fun)
Difficulty: 10/10 (from easy to Dark soul Mode)
Last but no least lets be logical this game is in early access and its really good for its price
A badass indie developer at it again with Rogue Legacy 2. Gives me the nostalgia of something oldschool like megaman while implementing new age roguelite elements.
With the Drifting Worlds patch, this game really stepped up - finding those fabled weapons makes each run that much more exciting!

If you liked the first one, then of course you'll like this one.

+ Much deeper story than the original, despite the humor attached to the classes and writing
+ Optional bosses are difficult and fun
+ Optional "options" where you can DM yourself and make the game even more difficult
+ First game had 4 worlds, this one has 6. Neat
+ Combat has an upgrade but still holds true to the original formula for the most part, minus new abilities
+ The best kind of Roguelite imo, that is to say, one with great/proper progression

- You have to beat the game 8 times to get all the of the Story. I think it would've been better to have all that extra Lore in the first NG+. Instead, they give it piece by piece and then force you to beat the game again and again in order to get the next juicy bit. And the extra lore is very juicy.

Yes

Anyone giving this a negative review is as disingenuous as it gets. I was real close to never playing this from some of these negative reviews. The review system is to guide fellow people "of interest" of the genre or type of game whether or not they should give it a go. NOT your butthurt opinion of not being able to beat a boss after 80 hours, or specific small issues. Anyone suggesting NEGATIVE review, meaning, do not play, is a jerk. Rude to the player and even moreso the developer. This game is super polished, fantastic, and expansive. Very much to do and NOT easy. You can always refund if its not for you, but to not give it a chance? blasphemy. get it on sale though, pretty steep for a roguelike at full price

Addictive, good progression, very fun if you like rogue-like games! It can get a bit grindy at later stages when you're trying to beat certain bosses and you need to max out your stats, or maybe I'm just not good enough to beat them without maxing out everything lol.

Great improvement and continuation on the formula of Rogue Legacy. Love all the additional classes. LOVE the inclusion of House Rules so I can play like a dumb two-button barbarian and not feel like I'm missing out too much.

RL2 is a fast paced roguelite that takes inspiration from Hollow Knight and Celeste.

It was initially released with about only 3 hours of content but now it's 10+ after the first big update. They also fixed a bunch of traits that were eye straining so now the random character selection feels better.

Overall I really enjoy it. Still a long way to go in EA but I really enjoy it. To me it feels like it's being a lot smarter about everything than RL1 in how they control more what type of movement skills you have access to so they can design the game around it rather than how it was when you could freely stack tons of dashes or tons of double jumps.

Game is still not completed and some stuff still needs sorting. When I first made this review there was a clunky feel to the dash into spin kick bounce but it got fixed days after I wrote that. So stuff is moving fast.
A little grindy in spots but if you think you're gonna like it you're gonna like it.

Grinding for upgrades/gold does not feel rewarding, and bosses can be easily killed by abusing chef. Needs more incentive and avenues to unlock upgrades rather than farming for gold. Most of the end-game upgrades are locked behind new game plus.

A really strong improvement on Rogue Legacy 1 with a large number of quality of life changes (my favourite being all blue spells go through walls and starting with the dash) and also new mechanics that feel unique and add their own challenges to them.

I personally don't use a number of the new classes that have been added but with the hero reroll unlocked that isn't an issue.
I didn't like the first game very much, but the gameplay improvements, class variety, and charming design make this one a pleasure to play. Would definitely recommend.
What an amazing sequel and stellar game. Many classes to play from warriors and wizards to cooks and boxers. Too many abilities to name. Buy it. Don't be a wimp.

One of the greatest games I have ever played. An amazing story as well as amazing gameplay. Some of the most challenging boss fights I've ever faced but I had fun through every second of it. I'm nowhere near done with this game and probably won't be for a long time. I recommend this game to quite literally everybody as even if you don't like the base gameplay, the house rules make it an enjoyable experience for anyone who plays. Enjoy! And remember to flip, that last step is a doozy..

Edit from 3 years later: Still my favorite game ever made. But to whichever asshole designed the dragon dream... Please die painfully. Thank you, that is all.
takes the original game, then expands and improves upon it in a lot of unique ways. Strong recommend if you're a fan of the original, or roguelikes in general

The first game is one of the best implementations I have played of the rogue genre.

This one is even better.
Great game idea. It has a lot of replayability and each run seems unique with random trinkets or traits, all classes seem balanced with each territory favore different class but all playable.
Fun and varied platforming, fair difficulty. Each area is completely different and requires adapting to the new way it is played.

The game really challenges you during boss fights as well as the maps with many enemies on screen, it helps you improve your reaction timings. Roguelike / Roguelite games are not easy to adapt to since they are mostly RNG for maps visited, however i can say after 28 hours of playing I have reached later maps on the game and ready to catch up to comig updates. Would recommend it to Roguelike / Roguelite fans and whomever likes to challenge him/her self.
You're probably gonna wanna wait this one out. Core mechanics are all there and that's it. You only get one level so it's very unfinished.

Rogue Legacy 2 is a rogue-like platformer game developed and published by Cellar Door Games. The game is the sequel to the popular Rogue Legacy game, and builds upon its predecessor with improved graphics, gameplay, and features.

One of the standout features of Rogue Legacy 2 is its unique blend of platforming and RPG elements. Players take on the role of a knight exploring procedurally generated dungeons, battling monsters and collecting treasure. The game's RPG mechanics allow players to level up their character, unlock new abilities, and customize their loadout to suit their playstyle.

Another standout feature of Rogue Legacy 2 is its challenging gameplay. The game is designed to be difficult, with punishing enemy encounters and traps that require quick reflexes and careful planning to overcome. However, the game's "rogue-lite" elements allow players to retain some progress even after death, allowing them to gradually improve and eventually conquer the game's toughest challenges.

The game's graphics and art style are also impressive, with a colorful and cartoonish aesthetic that is both charming and distinctive. The game's sound design is also top-notch, with an upbeat and engaging musical score that perfectly complements the game's fast-paced action.

Overall, Rogue Legacy 2 is an outstanding rogue-like platformer that builds upon the success of its predecessor with improved graphics, gameplay, and features. Its unique blend of platforming and RPG elements, challenging gameplay, and engaging graphics and sound design make it a standout title in the genre, and a must-play for fans of rogue-like games.

11.5 hrs:
The Far Shores update is really good, I think the game is definitely worth $20 at this point. They've done a decent job with balancing the classes. I still don't care much for using magic outside the Mage class and will not play Arrow-Shootman ever but the other 4 melee classes have different defensive options that will change how you play slightly in interesting ways. At this point I've encountered the second boss but haven't beaten him yet. There's supposedly a 3rd biome and boss but I think I have to beat #2 first to see them.

They're trying to make the game feel more roguelike and have said they're refining the artifact/trait systems. In the end this should give a good variation to character randomness at generation and interesting choices to make when picking up artifacts during your run.

If you liked the first game you will probably like this one too.
Early Access: They are working on things. The very first patch, two days after public release, addressed my two biggest concerns.

I played the original and beat it. This game is that and so much more. If you loved everything about rough legacy you will love this game. Every run goes different. The challenges, more challenging. And just an amazing game 100% recommend.
Everything I was hoping for as a rogue lite, a sequel to rogue legacy, and just all around a fun game.

Love this game. It's the perfect blend of elements that make a great rogue-lite. There's a lot of progress to be made via the castle building system, so each time you start a new run you're potentially stronger than the last time you went through. There's a lot of different classes to choose from, they're all pretty fun except the assassin... I don't like that one. You can even unlock the option to lock one of the 3 new hero selections as one preferred class, so you can guarantee that you have an assassin every time.

Well worth the price, excited to see the next content drop!

I like the game fun and cool i like the art style and overall a good game
this is classic 2d mario for 2023. a masterpiece. no run is the same. only 20 hours in but yeah its a blast.

Excellent game-feel, it's super duper tight and all the new class-unique attacks are awesome. If you mashed together a platformer, an action focused metroidvania with a dash of rogue-lite this is what you get. Worthy successor in mechanics, but as of right now there is very little content. Even as a early-access release you have to be prepared to only get a single digit amount of meaningful hours. Maxed out my castle in less than 4. So a lot is missing, but I adored the first game and I'm here to help support it's sequel!
After 100 hours I finally had a run where I cleared every single room and boss with a single character. Never had a better experience in a game. 10/10 GOTY

Better then the first part. Most importantly there are more game features and classes have more unique playstyle.
The same as in the first part -- very good arcade platform game.

Banger of a rogue like, pure fun, nice scaling that creates a real long and enjoyable play-through, many classes to master and mess around with ...

Def a good game !

Same addictive gameplay as the original, but with so much more depth -- more playable classes, more equipment, more runes, and 100s of levels of NG+, if that's your thing. Great combat, with balanced abilities and different playstyles for each class. (Some bosses are much easier if you choose a specific class specifically for the boss attempt.) The story isn't as clear as the first game, but that's the only complaint I have. Great game.

I've put a lot of hours into numerous roguelikes. I think what RL2 does really well is finding something to get excited about even in "failed" runs. There's always something you did, whether it was got money & exp to advance your castle, or maybe you unlocked a new teleporter, or unlocked a boss chamber. Little bits of progress everywhere. Perhaps what it does best is the variety of classes you can play as. They mostly all feel good, and while some are easier than others, the cost of doing a run with any character is so low that you're very encourage to experiment.

Postgame is excellent here too. It has a Hade's-like system where you choose how the game will get harder in future runs, which, if you're going to steal form Hade's, that is an excellent system to steal.

I've beaten the last boss after 30 hours of gameplay. Didn't encounter any bugs or technical difficulties whatsoever. it is a pretty good game i would say. I'll keep playing to see whats more to do after beating the boss. Also, the game is not as hard as Dead Cells for example, so its more accessible.

If you like the genre, give this one a try.
Literally better than the first one in ALMOST everyway. I was on the fence, however grab this game its definitely worth it!!!I don't review many games and the ones I do are worth taking a look at.

Fantastic roguelike with way more depth than expected and even more customization that the first. Absolutely wicked difficulty, but a great feeling of progression as you begin to level up your lineage, equip new armors, unlock multiple new types of character and more. Just fantastic and a great successor to the original!
This game is awesome!, its a combination of a roguelike and a metroidvaina and those are 2 of my fav!
i think this is an improvement over the first Rogue Legacy in all aspects. i have been playing it exclusively since i bought it and love it.
Genuinely a blast of a rogue-like, with solid meta progression and lots of silly stuff mixed in. Took me awhile to beat it the first time for sure, but worth every minute.

Pretty good roguelike with some cute progression mechanics but the learning curve is fairly steep. The dialogue is pretty funny and keeps things a bit fresh every run.Gets a little repetitive near the end but the NG+ options are there if you're into it.

I've been playing Rogue Legacy 2 since the August release. I had a lot of fun with it, but even being dynamically generated at the there just wasn't enough verity and depth to last more than a few hours. I still recommended it in that state, and a found out recently that I apparently had missed an update back in October. I decided to give the game one more go with the new update and WOW.

In comparison to the original there is much more depth to each character class, and I'm beginning to see how each character class can mature as you level them up. Also, the new version is beginning to include some truly unique game play mechanics. The kind that make me wonder, "How am I supposed to do that?" even after watching a walk-through video.

Bravo. Keep it coming!
